raw_response:
Eh, I'll tell you how I do it. Been farming this land 45 years, what works works.

**My wheat** — I put it in back in October like always, right after the maize come out. Used my own saved seed mostly, some I bought from the agricultural store in town, the usual kind everyone plants around here. Before planting I spread two bags of compound fertilizer per mu — that's the colored one, 50 jin a bag. My boy helped me with the planter we hired from the neighbor, cost me a bit but no way I'm doing 10 mu by hand at my age.

Now it's spring, the wheat is greening up. I'll water it soon from the well — costs money to run the pump, electric bill ain't cheap, but you got to. I'll water maybe two, three times before harvest, depends on the rain. When the wheat stands up tall at jointing I'll scatter half a bag of urea per mu, maybe a bit more if it looks yellow. If I see them little bugs on the heads later, I'll spray once. Weeds I already sprayed back in winter.

Harvest comes early June, I hire the combine — everyone does now, nobody cuts by hand no more. Straw gets chopped into the field.

**Then maize goes right in**, no time to rest the ground. Maybe one week turnaround, got to hurry. I buy hybrid seed every year, can't save it, that's how it is. Plant with the hired machine same as wheat. Put down a bag of compound at planting, then when the maize is knee-high I topdress urea, maybe 25-30 jin per mu. Water once or twice if June-July is dry, otherwise skip it — saves me money.

Maize harvest end of September, dry it on the road and the yard, sell some, keep some for the chickens and for us. Wheat mostly we keep for flour, sell what's left over.

Money's tight. My daughter-in-law works at the factory in town, that helps. I don't spend more on fertilizer than I have to — too much is waste, my father always said, and I seen plenty of folks throw good money away. I do what I done last year if last year was okay. Last year was okay.
